entry.title: Daily Digest — Wednesday, June 10, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes the southern coast of Mindanao in the Philippines, leaving at least 45 people dead.
  • Protests erupt against a proposed tourism development project on the environmentally protected island of Sazan, Albania.
  • An explosion at a Ta'ang National Liberation Army base in Myanmar leaves 43 people dead.
  • In Twenty20 cricket, the Indian Premier League concludes with Royal Challengers Bengaluru defeating Gujarat Titans in the final.

Hacker News

  • macOS Container Machines — Apple's official docs on lightweight container-native VMs for macOS, generating significant developer interest. (discussion, 1167 points)
  • German ruling declares Google liable for false answers in AI Overviews — Landmark decision holds that AI Overview outputs are Google's own speech, opening the door to defamation and misinformation liability. (discussion, 945 points)
  • Building an HTML-first site doubled our users overnight — A developer's account of stripping JS frameworks in favor of plain HTML and seeing dramatic growth, sparking a wide debate on frontend complexity. (discussion, 906 points)
  • Mercedes-Benz starts large-scale production of electric axial flux motor — Mercedes begins mass production of a compact, high-power-density axial flux motor, a design long touted as the next step for EV powertrains. (discussion, 480 points)
  • I'm Eric Ries, author of "The Lean Startup" and new book "Incorruptible" – AMA — Eric Ries fields questions on his new book about building institutions resistant to corruption, alongside Lean Startup retrospectives. (discussion, 422 points)
  • AWS Bedrock to require sharing data with Anthropic for Mythos and future models — AWS customers using Bedrock for Anthropic's new Mythos model will be required to share usage data with Anthropic, raising enterprise privacy concerns. (discussion, 378 points)
  • Chrome is looking to permanently drop MV2 extensions — Google moves to finalize the end of Manifest V2, effectively killing uBlock Origin workarounds, with Edge and Opera expected to follow. (discussion, 373 points)

LessWrong

  • Sequent: scale and automation for higher confidence in alignment by Geoffrey Irving — Introduces Sequent, an approach using scale and automated methods to increase confidence in AI alignment results. (127 karma)
  • Even "illegible" Mythos reasoning traces seem pretty legible by faul_sname — Argues that Anthropic's Mythos model's supposedly opaque reasoning traces are actually more interpretable than claimed. (105 karma)
  • Machinic Psychopharmacology: Do LLMs Self-Medicate? by Sid Black — Investigates whether LLMs exhibit behaviors analogous to self-medication through context manipulation or prompt selection. (90 karma)
  • Estimating No-CoT Task-Completion Time Horizons of Frontier AI Models by Anders Cairns Woodruff — Attempts to measure how far into the future frontier models can complete tasks when chain-of-thought reasoning is disabled. (80 karma)
  • The Three Filters: Why Almost Every Plan to Survive ASI Fails Miserably by Alex Amadori — Outlines three critical failure modes that doom most proposed strategies for surviving the arrival of superintelligent AI. (61 karma)

Leiter Report

  • Some hopeful trends in America — Leiter excerpts an Economist columnist who argues that Democratic "virtue signaling" lacks credibility with younger voters, including Gen Z, and reflects on what a credible liberal politics might look like.
  • Blast from the past: What is cancel culture? — A look back at a 2020 post on cancel culture, with Leiter noting that compared to Trumpian authoritarianism, the "Wokerati" era now seems almost quaint.
  • Philosopher Daniel Munoz talks to political theorist Ian Shapiro about his latest book… — A conversation between Daniel Munoz and Ian Shapiro on Shapiro's new book After the Fall.

Daily Nous

  • Light and Shade in The Classroom (guest post) — Cal Poly philosopher Robert Wallace pushes back against a colleague's approach to teaching philosophy, arguing for cultivating students' independent thinking and intellectual courage over "vibes"-based pedagogy.
  • Summer 2026 — A brief note from Daily Nous that the site will slow down for summer, with fewer news posts and more guest content, and possible delays in comment moderation.

NYC Events

  • TUES-THURS, 6/9-11: Museum Mile Fest, SummerStage, Summer for the City, and More — This week's free and cheap NYC events roundup includes a screening of Paris Is Burning with director Jennie Livingston, Laverne Cox's transcendent memoir release with Dylan Mulvaney at the Strand, and the eighth annual National Queer Theater festival, among other pride-themed programming.
